# Cached REST routes (the tier-2 catalogue)

One entry per cached REST route family: what it absorbs, the exact trimmed shape it rebuilds, its query-shape guard, and what invalidates it. Extracted verbatim from CLAUDE.md, which now carries only the contract and an index -- the depth lives here so it can grow.

The contract these all obey (show gate, absorb-and-rebuild, no URL keys, explicit invalidation) is in CLAUDE.md under "The cache contract (three tiers)". `GET /api/brief` on the dashboard renders the same checklist next to the traffic that is still uncached.

## The identical-or-passthrough rule (internal/api/proxy_test.go)

An endpoint is either served byte-identical to GitHub (from a verbatim cache, or a live forward) or it is not cached at all. Never a trimmed subset a consumer can read a dropped field from. `/user`, `/compare`, and `/pulls/{n}/files` were all, at different points, cached with a trim that broke or will break a consumer. Keeping the rule rather than relitigating it fixed each. `/compare` and `/pulls/{n}/files` are tier-2 routes whose rebuilds preserve the consumer-read fields exactly (`respcache_compare_test.go`, `respcache_pullfiles_test.go`). `/user` (and `/app`, `/user/orgs` alongside it) cache the upstream body VERBATIM, byte for byte, instead of guessing a field subset again -- see `respcache_identity_test.go`.

This is for the hit/miss byte-identity proof.

## The default JSON Accept

`acceptsDefaultJSON` (`internal/api/respcache.go`) decides which `Accept` a cached route serves. Every listed media range must be one of `*/*`, `application/*`, `application/json`, `application/vnd.github+json` or `application/vnd.github.v3+json`. The gh CLI sends `application/vnd.github.merge-info-preview+json, application/vnd.github.nebula-preview` on every request. Both previews are graduated and change no REST JSON body, so both count as the default too, with or without `+json`. Any other media type passes through as `unmodeled-accept`.

## The routes

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path...}` (incl. `?ref=`, part of the key) — absorbs 200 file (base64), 200 dir (trimmed entries), **and 404** (the "config file absent" answer is half the win). One global row per (owner, repo, path, ref). Invalidated per PUSHED REF (+ the empty-ref default-branch spelling) by `push`, repo-wide by `repository` — see the dispatcher bullet's per-ref matrix — plus a **24h TTL backstop**. A **submodule** entry is stored as its own kind, rebuilt as `{type, submodule_git_url, size, name, path, sha}`. `submodule_git_url` is a pinned exception on the hook `config.url` grounds: it is the identity of the submodule, not a link into the API.

  **The raw file-body Accept** (`Accept: application/vnd.github.raw`, `.raw+json`, or the legacy `.v3.raw` spelling — what simple-llm-ui's file-read tool sends, docs/tools/filesystem-tools.md in that repo) shares the SAME absorbed row as the default JSON shape: there is no second cache dimension. Base64-DECODING the already-absorbed `content` (`serveContentsRaw`) rather than caching a second copy servs a raw-Accept request. A miss is always fetched with the regardless of the DEFAULT JSON Accept of which shape the caller asked for. It mirrors go-github, PyGithub, and octokit.js.

  This all resolve file-vs-directory via the default JSON shape first and never send. The raw media type against a path that can be a directory (GitHub's behavior there is undocumented). `acceptsRawContents` requires every listed media range to be a raw one. An EMPTY Accept is deliberately NOT raw (`acceptsDefaultJSON` already claims that case, and the two stay mutually exclusive so the top-level gate never double-counts a request).

  The place this cannot be made to work — a file too large for the base64 JSON form (>1 MiB. GitHub answers `encoding:"none"` past that, only raw/object media types carry the bytes) — falls back to a second. This is UNCACHED `fetchUpstream` call with the caller's own raw Accept header, replayed verbatim (`replayUnstored`) rather than routed through the passthrough proxy's debouncer. This exists to price shapes this mirror can still learn to model, not ones that are structurally unabsorbable.

  `serveContentsRaw` decodes the stored base64 (stripping the embedded line breaks GitHub's MIME-style wrapping inserts, which are not part of the base64 alphabet) and serves the raw bytes with `Content-Type` fixed at `text/plain; charset=utf-8` rather than replaying GitHub's own (undocumented, weakly-evidenced) raw response type. Every known consumer of this shape (simple-llm-ui's file-read tool, agentic-loop's repo client) detects binary content by inspecting the BODY (UTF-8 validity / NUL bytes), not `Content-Type`. This must not see a `json`-containing `Content-Type` here.

  Agentic-loop's `IsDirectoryListing` treats any body starting with `[` under a json `Content-Type` as a directory listing. This will misidentify a text file whose content happens to start with `[`.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits/{sha}` (`respcache_gitcommits.go`) — positive rows are immutable: no invalidation, no TTL, LRU-bounded only. Rebuild: `{sha, author{...}, committer{...}, message, tree:{sha}, parents:[{sha},...]}`. **Push payloads feed this cache too** (`absorbPushCommits`): each pushed commit is upserted once, globally. Parents come from the payload's linear chain (`webhook.PushPayload.ChainedCommits`). This declines forced pushes, new refs, possibly-truncated arrays (≥20), and non-linear orderings rather than derive incorrect parents. A **404 is cached as an expiring MISS MARKER** (`git_commit_miss_cache`, rebuilt in the contents route's `{"message":...,"status":"404"}` shape, 24h TTL) — a round-2 stance change: round 1 deliberately did not cache these ("a missing sha can be pushed later"). However, the dominant traffic is pr-minder's `mergeWouldBeEmpty` re-reading GC'd test-merge shas forever, each read a fresh upstream 404. Bounds make it safe: the expiry, and the **clear-on-upsert invariant** — every real commit absorb (fetch, push payload, commits-list, compare) funnels through `ghdata.upsertGitCommit`. This clears the sha's marker. As a result, a materialized sha stops answering 404 immediately. Consumers fail open on 404 regardless.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits` — the commits LIST (behind show. Pr-minder's fork-point base detection pages this per branch, dozens per sweep — the passthrough flood that motivated the route). Absorb-do not-byte-cache: each listed commit is upserted into the SAME global `git_commits_cache` rows above. A `commits_list_cache` snapshot per exact modeled query shape — key `(owner, repo, ref_param, per_page, page)`, where `ref_param` is the raw `sha` query value (`''` = default branch).

  This is stores only the response's ordered shas (the rows+marker split the pulls list uses). A hit needs an unexpired snapshot AND every listed sha still resolving in `git_commits_cache` (an LRU-pruned commit degrades to a miss, self-healing. The re-absorb restores the pair).

  Hit and miss rebuild the same trimmed item `{sha, commit:{author{name,email,date}, committer{...}, message, tree:{sha}}, parents:[{sha},...]}` — a superset of the field the consumers (pr-minder `listCommitShas` + the reconcile hook's port) actually read (the top-level `sha`. They paginate by short-page detection, no Link header). The top-level author/committer USER objects, `node_id`, `verification`, `comment_count`, and every URL field stay dropped.

  Query-shape guard: only `sha` (non-empty), `path` (non-empty, bounded), `per_page` (1..100, default 30) and `page` (1..10, default 1) are modeled. Anything else (`since`, `until`, `author`, ...) or a non-default `Accept` passes through. A `path`-filtered page is not a prefix of the ref's history. It is its own whole stored page on `repo_answer_cache` (kind `commits_path`). Its subject is the `sha` value. A 404 for a named `sha` is the unknown-ref verdict, stored on the same table (kind `commits_verdict`). Both drop on the commits list's own per-ref push flush, and on a create or delete of the ref. Unlike the pulls list there is NO full-page truncation guard. The snapshot IS that exact page's answer, and pagination continues under the next page's own key. Only a 200 absorbs (an empty array — a page past the end — is a valid cacheable answer).

  404 (unknown ref), 409 (empty repo), 5xx relay unstored. Push flushes snapshots`, repo-wide by `repository`, + a 24h TTL backstop. The single commit read `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}` is a different shape with its own entry below.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{basehead}` — the three-dot `base...head` comparison (behind show. Pr-minder's `compareCommits` — the `auto_open_pr` open gate + `closeEmptyAutoPrs`, repeated fleet-wide every few minutes by the pr-minder-reconcile hook. This is the ~90%-of-request-log passthrough flood that motivated the route). HISTORY: an earlier /compare cache was REMOVED because its trim dropped `files`, breaking pr-minder's empty-PR gate — this rebuild keeps every consumer-read field.

  `{status, ahead_by, behind_by, total_commits, merge_base_commit:{sha}, commits:[<the commits-list trimmed item shape>], files:[{filename, status, additions, deletions, changes, previous_filename?}]}` with the **files array's presence/absence preserved exactly** (consumers read `changed_files = files.length`. ABSENT = unknown → fail open, EMPTY = 0-diff → the close-empty gate) and the unread per-file `patch` never stored. The route is greedy (`compare/*` — branch names carry slashes). The whole trimmed doc is stored per exact `(owner, repo, basehead)` in `compare_cache`.

  The row also splits `base_ref`/`head_ref` into their own columns (round 2), which is what enables the per-ref flush. The compare's commits are also upserted into `git_commits_cache` (synergy. A hit never depends on those rows). This repo's pushes) or without `...` → passthrough models Shape guard: NO query params.

  A 200 absorbs the comparison. A **404 absorbs as an unknown-ref VERDICT** (a status-404 row, `{"message":...,"status":"404"}` doc — the fleet's close-empty pass compares `base...head` for fork PRs whose head ref does not exist in the base repo, a 404 repeated every sweep by design). 5xx relays unstored.

  A comparison (or verdict) depends on both refs' tips/existence, so a `push` flushes every row naming the pushed ref on EITHER side (`base_ref`/`head_ref` match. Ref creation/deletion arrives as a push, so a verdict clears the moment its missing ref is created). `repository` flushes repo-wide (covering renames), plus the 24h TTL backstop.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/status` + `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/check-runs` + the raw statuses LIST — served under BOTH its path spellings: the legacy alias **`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{ref}`** (what the consumers actually send — required-builds' `listStatuses`. A GET-only top-level `statuses/*` registration whose wildcard is the whole possibly-slashed ref. As a result, the required-builds status PUBLISH `POST /statuses/{sha}` falls to MethodNotAllowed → the proxy, pinned by a regression test) and the modern `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/statuses` subtree form. Both land in ONE handler and ONE row space.

  All kinds are whole-document snapshots in ONE table (`commit_ci_cache`, a `kind` column: `status`/`check_runs`/`statuses_list`), keyed by the VERBATIM `{ref}` (a branch name — slashes and all. This is a sha, or a tag. NEVER resolved, so each spelling is its own row) **+ `per_page`/`page`** (round 2: required-builds paginates check-runs and raw statuses at `per_page=100&page=N`. This is until a short page, so pagination joined the key — `per_page` 1..100 default 30, `page` 1..10 default 1, parsed like the PR-files route.

  The check-runs filters `check_name`/`status`/`filter`/`app_id`, repeated params, and out-of-range paging still pass through). The status/check-runs pair is registered as a `/commits/*` subtree dispatcher whose trailing-literal suffix anchor (`.../status`, `.../check-runs`, `.../statuses`) is what lets a ref carry slashes. A single-segment `{ref}` route parameter can never match one. Every OTHER tail (the single-commit read, `/check-suites`, `/pulls`, ...) is forwarded to the passthrough proxy unchanged.

  Trimmed rebuilds: status = `{state, sha, total_count, statuses:[{context, state, description, created_at, updated_at}]}` (nullable `description` preserved. `sha` is the RESOLVED tip the answer described — exactly why pushes must flush branch-form rows). Check-runs = `{total_count, check_runs:[{id, head_sha, name, status, conclusion, started_at, completed_at, app:{id}, output:{title}, details_url, html_url}]}` (nullable conclusion/started_at/completed_at preserved — consumers branch on conclusion===null. `app` trimmed to its id, the own-check filter field. `output` ALWAYS emitted but trimmed to exactly `{title: string|null}` — never the unbounded summary/text).

  Statuses-list = a BARE JSON ARRAY of `{context, state, description, target_url, created_at, updated_at}` preserving response order EXACTLY (required-builds dedups by context FIRST-WINS relying on newest-first) with description/target_url nullable but always keyed. The blanket "no link fields" rule became a **pinned-allowlist mechanism** (the 2026-07-11 consumer survey superseded 2026-07-05's). The no-URL test takes an exact-key allowlist per route, and the per-status `target_url` + per-run `details_url`/`html_url` are pinned. This is consumer-read exceptions (required-builds renders all three on its breakdown page).

  Adding another exception requires a fresh survey. Still dropped: per-status ids/creator, per-run `url`/node_id/external_id/check_suite/pull_requests and output's summary/text. Absorb gate: a 200 whose body carries its array (statuses / check_runs / the bare array) absorbs. An empty statuses array is cacheable. The 404 unknown-ref VERDICT is absorbed too (the compare_cache precedent): a fine-grained-PAT caller polling check-runs/status/statuses for a sha that never resolves.

  This is re-earns the same 404 on every sweep (this was, by measured volume, ~96% of the mirror's entire uncached traffic before this existed — see the implementation brief). It stays honest exactly like a 200 row: the same per-ref/per-repo flushes above cover it, and the 24h TTL backstops missed deliveries. A 403 is the caller's OWN credential lacking a scope, not a fact about the ref. It is never written to this table, which has no actor column. It is stored per principal in the deny cache instead (`respcache_verdicts.go`), so the polling credential stops reaching GitHub and no other credential sees it. `page` is modeled up to 40.

  This table carries no actor column, so caching a credential-scoped denial will serve it to a differently-scoped caller (an App installation token, say) who can get. This is a real answer from the exact same request. 5xx relay unstored. These routes deliberately do NOT read or write the `commit_checks` truth table: its normalized per-context rows are lossy against these responses (no timestamps, descriptions, or run ids). Unifying the representations is possible future work.

  Invalidation is the load-bearing part: `status`/`check_run`/`check_suite` events flush the payload-named refs' rows. The head branch(es) + the sha itself, every kind, every page (repo-wide when the payload names none) — `push` flushes the pushed ref's rows, and `repository` flushes repo-wide. As a result, snapshots only survive while a ref's CI is quiet. This is exactly when the fleet sweeps re-poll them. 24h TTL backstop.
- `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` — the token-mint cache, registered OUTSIDE requireAuth (an App JWT cannot resolve `GET /user`): the handler verifies the bearer itself via `ghclient.VerifyAppIdentity` and keys by the app principal. Key: (app id, installation id, SHA-256 of the **canonicalized** request body). Only a 201 whose `expires_at` parses is stored, served until `expires_at - 10min`. Rebuild is exactly `{token, expires_at, permissions?, repository_selection?}`. Invalidated on `installation`/`installation_repositories` events. An unverifiable bearer forwards unchanged, uncached. NOT global truth — a minted token is per-credential. **A CONSUMER App's installation webhooks never reach gsm**, so a 401/403 from GitHub on a proxied call carrying the minted token is the only signal. The cached mint's grants went stale. It drops the mint so the next mint refetches, while rate-limit refusals and foreign bearers leave it alone.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` — the open-PR list (behind show), absorbed into (and rebuilt from) the SAME global `pull_requests`/`pr_labels` tables the webhooks maintain — no separate state table. Serving a LIST from rows needs a completeness proof.

  As a result, a per-repo GLOBAL **"open-PR list complete" marker** (`pulls_list_cache`) gates it: set when an *unfiltered page-1* response absorbs with fewer items than `per_page` (which also reconciles cached open rows the response no longer contains, guarded by the fetch-start grace so a webhook racing the fetch wins). **cleared by `repository` events**. **never touched by `pull_request` events** — those maintain the rows, which is the point (a 24h TTL backstop bounds missed deliveries).

  A GraphQL sync can add rows that LACK the REST-only columns. The rebuild-time `allRestComplete` gate turns that into a miss rather than serving a hole. As a result, the marker needs no clearing there. Query-shape guard: only `state=open`, `per_page` (1..100), `page=1`, `head=owner:branch`, and `base=<branch>` are modeled — anything else passes through.

  `head` and `base` are pure FILTERS over the open set the marker already vouches for (given the whole open set, selecting by head or base is exactly what GitHub does). As a result, they are answered from state and, like any filtered response, not SET the marker. The base branch always lives in this repo, so its bare name is the whole filter, unlike `head`, which can name a fork.

  Pagination guard: a rebuilt list as long as the request's `per_page` is never served from state. Rebuilt item shape (trimmed, exactly a superset of what pr-minder + the pr-minder-reconcile hook read): `{node_id, number, state, title, user{login,type}, body, labels[{name,color}], created_at, updated_at, merge_commit_sha, draft, auto_merge (null | {merge_method}), head{ref,sha,repo:{full_name}|null}, base{ref,sha}}`.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}` — the single-PR read (behind show), served from a `pull_requests` row ONLY when the row is **rest-complete** (`ghdata.PRRestComplete`: node_id + base sha present — GraphQL-sourced rows never are), **recently touched** (`ghdata.PRRowFresh`, the 24h staleness backstop for a missed `closed` delivery — `touched_at` is bumped by every webhook/absorb). Its **`mergeable` is KNOWN** (MERGEABLE/CONFLICTING) **AND its `mergeable_state` is known and current** (non-empty, not `unknown`). `mergeable_state` is part of the gate rather than a field that rides along.

  This is because a CI event un-resolves it alone (unstable/blocked <-> clean moves no tip). Without this a row will keep hitting and serving a state GitHub has since left. As a result, a hit must mean every merge answer in the document is one GitHub currently stands behind. Its **diff stats are known** (`diffStatsKnown`: additions + deletions both non-NULL). GitHub and pr-minder polls it to resolution computes mergeable`.

  The known-mergeable gate is what makes caching safe — a null/unknown mergeable ALWAYS misses (fetch + absorb GitHub's computed answer, where a fetched null OVERWRITES via `SetPRMergeable` rather than COALESCE, so the poll keeps reaching GitHub until it resolves). A **branch push un-resolves** `mergeable` on affected open PRs (`NullPRMergeableByBranch`). A fetched CLOSED answer still DELETES any cached open row — the open-only invariant of `pull_requests` is untouched. However, it is now ABSORBED as a rendered whole-doc snapshot in `closed_pull_cache`.

  It served from it thereafter (every pr-minder drain re-reads settled PRs. Each such read used to be a fresh passthrough). The closed doc is the open rebuild's exact shape plus GitHub's real `merged` and its `mergeable` (key always present. Typically null), `state` exactly `"closed"` — consumers short-circuit on `pr.state !== 'open'` and read nothing else from a closed PR.

  EVERY `pull_request`/`pull_request_review` event (a reopen must not serve the stale doc flushes it. The REST open absorb also drops it), repo-wide by `repository`, bounded by a 24h TTL — and deliberately NOT flushed by `push` (a push cannot mutate a closed PR). A missed `reopened` delivery can therefore serve the stale closed doc for ≤24h — the same accepted staleness class as `PRRowFresh`, in the opposite direction.

  Any query string and non-numeric `{number}` segments pass through, as does any non-default `Accept` EXCEPT the diff read (next paragraph). Open rebuild = the + of the list item shape `{merged: false, mergeable: bool|null, additions: int|null, deletions: int|null}`. **`additions`/`deletions` ride the SINGLE rebuild only** — GitHub's list omits them, so emitting them on a rebuilt list item will invent numbers. No upstream answer supplied.

  The columns have always been absorbed (COALESCEd, so a later list/webhook write cannot blank them) and were simply never served, which is why repo-nightmare read them as `undefined` off the mirror. Nullable-but-always-keyed like `mergeable` (a fabricated `0` reads as "empty PR"), and the `diffStatsKnown` hit gate is what keeps that null off the wire in steady state. A row absorbed from the LIST has no stats while a webhook can resolve its `mergeable` independently.

  As a result, this is without the gate such a row will hit and serve `"additions": null` forever with nothing short of a push. This is to heal it. One miss re-absorbs the stats. Every later read hits.

  **Merge-field invalidation semantics** (mergeable + merge_commit_sha): a push to a PR's **base or head ⇒ both fields are stale** — GitHub recomputes lazily. GitHub never webhooks the result, so `NullPRMergeableByBranch` nulls them AND **remembers the nulled test-merge sha** (`merge_stale_sha`/`merge_stale_at`). A tip change ALWAYS changes the sha of a SUCCESSFUL test merge. A conflicted PR retains its last-good sha and re-offers it with `mergeable:false`.

  So **an absorb re-offering the remembered sha with mergeable true/unknown is presumed pre-push and can never re-resolve the row**. This is it stores (and the route serves) unresolved. The row keeps missing — each miss re-triggering GitHub's recompute — until a NEW sha arrives.

  This resolves and clears the marker (the guard lives in `UpsertPullRequest`'s SQL + `AbsorbSinglePull`, covering the single/list/webhook/sync writers uniformly. The marker rejects only within `ghdata.MergeStaleTTL` ≈ 1h == the strftime `'-1 hour'` cutoffs in the SQL, so a sha incorrectly marked stale. This is absorbed post-recompute before a late push delivery — cannot wedge the row into missing forever. The 24h row TTL stays the outer backstop).

  The marker also records the **push-tip proof** (`merge_stale_ref`/`merge_stale_after` — the pushed branch and its `after` tip, overwritten by every marking push. NULL when the payload had no usable after): an absorb whose reported tip for that branch equals the push's after sha provably post-dates. This is the push and is **accepted even when it re-offers the remembered sha**, so a Incorrect mark — the fresh post-push answer absorbed.

  This is before the late push delivery landed, then stamped stale by it — heals on the very next poll. A CONFLICTING same-sha answer is instead accepted once the marker outlives `ghdata.MergeStaleConflictingWindow` (30s, the SQL `'-30 seconds'` cutoffs — the dirty-retained pattern: the conflicted PR's frozen base.sha means the tip proof can never fire, and past replica lag the retained sha is the only explanation). As a result, conflicted PRs do not wedge to null after every base push.

  The `MergeStaleTTL` window is only the backstop for answers that never demonstrate either. Closed holes (the webhooks#66 frozen-sha incident — a hit never reaches GitHub, so nothing triggered the recompute): the push handler once ran `SetRepoPushedAt` FIRST and returned on its error, skipping the invalidation (it now runs first, each step logs-and-continues). An unparseable push payload skipped it fully (now: repo-wide `NullPRMergeableByRepo`, deliberately marker-less — the moved branch is unknown and an unmoved PR's re-offered sha is valid).

  And a recompute-lag refetch can re-resolve the just-invalidated sha permanently — while the sha-less GraphQL owner sync can re-arm `mergeable`. This is via COALESCE on a null/stale-sha REST row (now gated. Pure GraphQL rows keep sync-fed mergeable for the /graphql tier).

  **Two narrower un-resolvers cover what a branch/repo-wide push cannot.** `NullPRMergeableOnTipMove` un-resolves ONE PR's merge fields when an incoming webhook doc reports a moved tip against the stored row. The head sha changed (`synchronize` — including fork heads, which emit no push webhook to run the per-branch un-resolve) or the base ref was retargeted. The payload's own moved-side ref+sha become the marker proof, exactly the push-path semantics.

  As a result, the following upsert's stale guard treats the retained pre-move merge fields the payload carries as stale. drift of the Base ref. OID alone never triggers. This is because a conflicted PR's payload freezes `base.sha` at the last clean evaluation. As a result, OID comparison will false-positive on every dirty PR. Without a usable proof tip it stamps the marker without proof columns (the TTL backstop still bounds it) rather than a half-filled proof.

  `NullPRMergeableStateByHeadSHA` un-resolves `mergeable_state` ALONE for the open PRs on a head sha whose CI moved. This is a check or status result is the only thing that flips unstable/blocked ↔ clean. It moves no tip. As a result, this is the merge field with no other invalidator. `mergeable` and `merge_commit_sha` stay put, since a check result cannot change whether trees conflict.

  No stale marker is set either, because the marker refuses a re-offered PRE-PUSH test-merge sha and nothing pushed here. An empty sha (a payload naming none) is a no-op rather than a repo-wide wildcard — the caller has already flushed what it can.

  The **diff read's verdicts** (`respcache_pulldiff.go`): an Accept that is EXACTLY one media range naming the unified diff (`application/vnd.github.diff` or `.v3.diff`. Multi-range Accepts keep the plain passthrough) gets its own flow — pr-minder's `getPullDiff` sends exactly that. Pr-minder's `getP branches ONLY on ok/406 (406 = "diff too large" → the files-API fallback. Survey 2026-07-11), re-earning the same 406 on every describe hand-off for an oversized PR. The 406 VERDICT is cached per PR (`pull_diff406_cache`, doc `{"message": ...}`, served status 406) behind the SAME `pull` key of the resource of the deny kind + as the JSON read (same underlying resource, same authorization). A **200 diff BODY is stored VERBATIM** on `repo_answer_cache` (kind `pull_diff`, subject the PR number), under the identical-or-passthrough rule above: an opaque diff has no state to absorb, so it is served byte for byte with GitHub's `application/vnd.github.diff` type. That was the `unmodeled-response` slice of the 2026-10-12 brief. A diff over 1 MiB relays unstored. It shares the 406 verdict's flushes and TTL. Other statuses.

  Every other status relay unstored, every time.

  Flushed per PR by `pull_request`/`pull_request_review` (a head push can shrink the diff back under the boundary), repo-wide by `push`/`repository` (a BASE push can move any PR's three-dot diff across the boundary, with no per-PR signal), + 24h TTL.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation` — the App-level repo-installation lookup (pr-minder's `repoInstallationId`), registered OUTSIDE requireAuth exactly like the mint (App-JWT bearer, self-verified, app principal. `repo_installation_cache` table). Rebuild: `{id, account{login,type}, repository_selection, app_id, app_slug, target_type}`. Invalidated on `installation`/`installation_repositories` events by the stored installation id, plus a 24h TTL. 404 ("not installed") is never stored.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/files` — the PR files listing (behind show. Pr-minder's `assembleDiffFromFiles` pages it when GitHub 406s a too-large unified diff around a describe hand-off — the single largest passthrough slice. This is ~34%, before this route). Whole-doc per-page snapshots in `pull_files_cache`, keyed `(owner, repo, number, per_page, page)`.

  Trimmed per-file item `{filename, status, additions, deletions, changes, previous_filename?, patch?}` with the PRESENCE of `previous_filename` and `patch` preserved exactly (consumers test `typeof f.patch === 'string'`. GitHub legitimately omits `patch` on binary/oversized files) and the per-file blob `sha` + every URL field dropped. `patch` is unbounded, so a rendered document larger than **1 MiB passes through unstored** (the contents route's cap rule. The 8 MiB fetch cap still bounds the raw body).

  Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100, default 30) and `page` (1..**40**, default 1 — GitHub's files API stops at 3000 files = 30 pages at the consumers' `per_page=100`, plus margin for the trailing empty page. Smaller per_page shapes. Raised from 10 in round 2, deeper pages still pass through) only. Unknown/repeated params, a non-numeric `{number}` (`/pulls/comments/...`), or a non-default Accept pass through. Only a 200 absorbs, all-or-nothing. An empty array (a page past the end) is a valid cacheable answer.

  Flushed per PR by EVERY `pull_request`/`pull_request_review` event (head pushes — including fork heads whose push events never arrive — base retargets, reopens), repo-wide by `push`/`repository` (the belt for missed PR deliveries), + 24h TTL.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches` — the branches listing (behind show. Pr-minder's `listBranchHeads` feeds auto_open_pr fork-point detection, repeated fleet-wide by the reconcile hook — ~18% of passthroughs before this route). Whole-doc per-page snapshots in `branches_list_cache`, keyed `(owner, repo, per_page, page)`. Trimmed item `{name, commit:{sha}, protected}` (consumers read `name` + `commit.sha`. `protected` rides along as an always-present bool) with `commit.url`, the protection object, and `protection_url` dropped. Same shape guard as the files route (`per_page`/`page` only). The single-branch `/branches/{branch}` read is a different shape and stays passthrough. Only a 200 absorbs. Empty array cacheable. Branch create, delete, and tip-move all arrive as push events, so `push`/`repository` flush repo-wide, + 24h TTL. A tip-move is applied into the stored pages from the push's own `after` (`ghdata.ApplyPushedBranchTip`). Only membership changes flush the snapshots. No doc-size cap: the item shape has no unbounded field, and the 8 MiB `fetchUpstream` cap already bounds the raw body.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` (`respcache_actionsruns.go`) — TWO request shapes, served different ways, because they have different invalidation signals and the signal decides the design.
  - The **per-commit** shape `?head_sha=<sha>` (behind show. Survey 2026-07-11: pr-minder's `hasWorkflowRuns` sends `?head_sha=<hex>&per_page=1` and reads ONLY `total_count` — the zombie probe, repeated fleet-wide. This is required-builds' `listWorkflowRuns` pages `?head_sha=<hex>&per_page=100&page=N` reading name/status/conclusion/html_url). A sha is a accurate flush key. As a result, this stays a whole-doc snapshot in `workflow_runs_cache` keyed `(owner, repo, head_sha, per_page, page)`, flushed per sha by `status`/`check_run`/`check_suite`/`workflow_job` and repo-wide. This is by `repository`, 24h TTL. A `workflow_run` delivery instead **rewrites** the run's entry in place (`ghdata.ApplyWorkflowRunToPages`) — it IS the object these pages list. A run is updated in place upstream. Creation (measured orders the listing. See docs/webhooks/invalidations.md), so the entry cannot move. It falls back to the per-sha flush for a run the pages do not list, which is a new run only. A fetch can settle.
  - The repo-wide **LISTING** `?status=<s>&branch=<b>` — the GHA runner coordinator's queued-backlog poll, which at 46k forwards was 78% of ALL passthrough traffic. This is the largest single uncached slice the log has ever shown. This answer names no sha, so no delivery can flush it accurately. And clearing the repo's listings on every job event is invalidate-and-refetch, which the doctrine forbids outright. **So it is not a snapshot at all: it is rebuilt from the `workflow_runs` TRUTH table**.

    This the dispatcher maintains ONE TIME of the RUN AT A (`onWorkflowRun` applies the whole object. A `workflow_job` delivery establishes its run's identity and raises its status floor). A run entering or leaving `queued` changes this answer by updating one row, with every other run still served. `TestCachedWorkflowRuns_ListingTracksAppliedRunState` pins exactly that, and `TestDispatch_RunStateEvents_NeverClearTheListing` pins that no run delivery clears anything. Rows alone never prove a list.

    As a result, the listing is gated on a **completeness proof** (`workflow_runs_list_cache`, the `pulls_list_cache` pattern): one row per `(owner, repo, canonical filter set)` recording that a page-1 response. This is for exactly that filter came back SHORT, which is what proves truth then held every matching run. The same short answer RECONCILES — a row still matching the filter that the response omitted has provably moved. As a result, it goes.

    GitHub's listing trails its own `workflow_run.requested` delivery. An answer fetched just after the delivery omits the run it announced. A row touched within `ghdata.WorkflowRunListingLag` of the fetch start is therefore newer than the answer: reconcile keeps it. The answer is behind truth. Such an answer is relayed but records no completeness proof, and on the per-commit shape no snapshot. The next read fetches again.

    `TestCachedWorkflowRuns_AnswerBehindDeliveryNotStored` pins this.

    A run delivery MAINTAINS the rows and therefore must never touch the marker. Only `repository` events and its own short expiry (`ghdata.WorkflowRunsListTTL`, 2 min) clear it. That expiry bounds exactly one hole: a run entering the set with NO delivery naming it, which needs the App subscribed to `workflow_run`. A run with no jobs yet emits no `workflow_job` — and a queued backlog is what a coordinator provisions against. As a result, it is held to minutes rather than hours.

    Shape guard (both shapes): `head_sha` full hex lowercase-normalized. `status` one of GitHub's documented values. `branch` a bounded, control-character-free ref name. `per_page` 1..100. `page` 1..10. The modeled filters are canonicalized (sorted, escaped) so reordering a query string cannot mint a second proof.

    **The `status` filter matches a run's status OR its CONCLUSION**, because GitHub's does — `?status=success` selects completed runs that succeeded, and matching only. The status column will answer it with nothing. Every other filter (`event`/`actor`/`created`/`exclude_pull_requests`/...) is unmodeled and passes through. Deeper `/actions/runs/{id}/...` paths never reach the exact-literal registration and keep falling to the NotFound proxy.

    Rebuild (same from either source — one `renderWorkflowRuns`, so a hit and a miss cannot drift): `{total_count, workflow_runs:[{id, name, head_sha, status, conclusion, html_url, created_at, updated_at, run_started_at}]}`. On a miss `total_count` is copied VERBATIM from upstream (GitHub's TOTAL matching count, NOT the page length — exactly what the `per_page=1` probe reads). On a truth rebuild it is the filtered row count, exact.

    This is because the marker vouches for the set. name/conclusion/run_started_at are nullable with keys always emitted (truth stores `''` for "not reported" and renders it as null). `html_url` is a pinned consumer-read allowlist exception. Dropped: `node_id`, the `head_branch`/`event`/`actor`/`repository`/`head_commit` objects, every other `*_url`, and the unbounded `pull_requests`/`referenced_workflows` arrays. The trimmed shape lives in the store, so a `workflow_run` delivery's rewrite and the render agree byte for byte. Absorb gate: 200 + object + `total_count` and `workflow_runs` both PRESENT.

    Per run id > 0, non-empty status, full-hex head_sha. The zero-runs answer is cacheable — it IS the zombie probe's verdict. Every listed run enters truth whichever shape asked for it, so per-commit fetches keep the listing's rows warm for free. Run DELETION emits no webhook at all and is what both expiries are for.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}` (`respcache_actionsrun.go`) — the single run read, the largest passthrough in the 2026-10-12 brief. The gh CLI's `run view` and `run watch` send it with `?exclude_pull_requests=true`, and `gh wait-ci` sends it bare. **There is no snapshot.** The answer is rebuilt from the `workflow_runs` TRUTH row, the same row the repo-wide listing reads. The columns hold the state the listing needs. The run's `workflow_run_details` row holds the rest of the run object as JSON, ordered by the run's own `updated_at`. Only a source that carries the whole object writes it: a `workflow_run` delivery, or this route's own fetch. A job delivery or a listing absorb never touches it.

  A `workflow_run` delivery therefore APPLIES the run: the read serves the new state without a fetch. A run the mirror only heard about by delivery is served with no fetch at all. Freshness reads `detail_at`, the time a whole object last landed, not `touched_at`. This is because a job delivery moves `touched_at` but proves nothing about the run as a whole. A completed run serves for `ghdata.WorkflowRunSettledTTL` (24h, the lost re-run delivery bound). An unfinished run serves for `ghdata.WorkflowRunLiveTTL` (1 min, the lost transition bound).

  A miss fetches WITHOUT the query, applies the object to truth through the same `updated_at` ordering a delivery uses. And renders the row it reads back. A delivery that landed first therefore wins. `exclude_pull_requests` is modeled (`true`/`false`) and only empties `pull_requests` at render time. Any other parameter, a non-numeric id, or a non-default Accept passes through. Rebuild: `{id, name, node_id, head_branch, head_sha, path, display_title, run_number, event, status, conclusion, workflow_id, check_suite_id, html_url, pull_requests, created_at, updated_at, actor, run_attempt, run_started_at, triggering_actor, jobs_url, head_commit, repository, head_repository}`.

  Accounts trim to `{login, id, type}`, repositories to `{id, name, full_name, private, owner}`, pull requests to `{id, number, head, base}` with `{ref, sha, repo:{id, name}}` sides.

  **Pinned URL exceptions: `html_url` and `jobs_url`.** Consumer survey 2026-10-12: the gh CLI (`pkg/cmd/run/shared`) reads `html_url` for its link, and its `GetJobs` FOLLOWS `jobs_url` to list the run's jobs. `gh wait-ci` reads `html_url`. Every other `*_url` is dropped. A **403** is GitHub refusing this credential the run (4207 of the brief's answers, a token without `actions: read`). It is stored as a per-principal deny verdict, and so is a 404.

  Both are served from the deny cache for `ghdata.DenyTTL`. The verdict check runs after the show gate, because a readable repo is exactly the case where the gate admits the caller. 5xx relays unstored.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` — the bare repository read (behind show. The reconcile hook's `getDefaultBranch`, plus status-only access checks in the buildhost `canAccessRepo` style, where the 200-vs-404 IS the answer). UNLIKE every other cached route there is NO snapshot table and NO per-row TTL. The rebuild comes straight from the `repos` TRUTH row — the same webhook-maintained, fleet-synced, consistency-checked state tier multiple serves.

  So truth freshness IS the freshness model (mirroring how `/graphql` serves truth. `repository` events correct rename/delete/visibility, and a show probe re-absorbs the row per principal within the ≤24h grant TTL. This bounds how stale a private repo's row can sit for a probing caller).

  Served only when the row can answer Fully: known visibility (unknown `''` fails CLOSED — e.g. a row seeded only by the identity-locked GraphQL fetch, which carries no visibility), a known `default_branch`, and a canonical full name. Anything else fetches with the caller's token and the absorbed heals the row. Trimmed rebuild: `{name, full_name, owner:{login}, private, visibility, default_branch, archived, disabled}` — `private` derived (visibility != public, so `internal` folds to private=true).

  `pushed_at` deliberately NOT emitted (truth `''` cannot distinguish never-pushed from not-yet-synced, and no consumer reads it). `fork`/`id` not stored, so not emitted. Query params, non-default Accepts, and HEAD requests (MethodNotAllowed → the proxy) pass through. A non-200 fetch relays unstored.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/{ref...}` (`respcache_gitrefs.go`) — the ref-to-tip lookup ("where does this branch point right now"), the largest UNROUTED slice of the request log before it existed. This is fleet reconcile passes ask it per branch, forever. The wildcard is greedy (a ref path is at least `heads/<name>` and branch names carry slashes) and the ref is stored **VERBATIM, not resolved** — `heads/main` and `refs/heads/main` are distinct requests.

  As a result, each is its own row and the push flush covers every spelling (`refSpellings`). Rebuild: `{ref, node_id, object:{sha, type}}` — the canonical ref name GitHub reported, a stable identifier, and the object trimmed to sha + type. `url` and `object.url` dropped. Shape guard: no query parameter changes this answer so any is unmodeled. The ref must be a fully-qualified two-part ref (`heads/<name>`, `tags/<name>`, with or without the `refs/` prefix).

  GitHub answers a PARTIAL ref (`heads`) with an ARRAY, a different shape this route does not hold. The **404 is absorbed as a VERDICT** on the compare route's precedent (sweeps re-poll deleted heads — a merged PR's head — forever). It cannot outlive the ref: ref creation arrives as a push for that exact ref, which drops the row. Freshness: a `push` **APPLIES its own `after` tip** to the row in every spelling (`ghdata.ApplyPushedRefTip`) — the payload states the answer.

  As a result, nothing is refetched and the row is never briefly absent. It falls back to the per-ref DELETE only where the payload cannot answer. A deletion (all-zeros `after`), a cached 404 verdict a creation must clear (no `node_id` in a push payload to build a real answer from), or an unreadable row. Repo-wide delete by `repository` and by a push naming no usable ref. The 24h TTL is now only the backstop for a delivery that never landed.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` and `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}` (`respcache_workflowjobs.go`). Both share one `workflow_jobs_cache` row space under the kinds `run_jobs` and `job`. **A job still moving is stored too, and its own deliveries keep it fresh.** A queued or running job is a live value the GHA runner coordinator provisions against. No TTL is short enough to be safe and long enough to be worth having. A TTL is the incorrect instrument.

  A `workflow_job` delivery carries the whole job object, so the FETCH proves a page's membership (which jobs belong to the run. Nothing in a delivery says "and that is all of them") and the DELIVERIES rewrite each entry as the job moves (`ghdata.ApplyWorkflowJob`). The TTL is then the lost-delivery bound, three-way because one part of the answer no delivery keeps current. GitHub sends one delivery per job TRANSITION while a RUNNING job's `steps` advance between them unreported.

  Settled 24h, jobs merely WAITING `WorkflowJobsQueuedTTL` 60s (a queued job's steps are empty by construction, so a rewritten entry is exactly right), a job RUNNING `WorkflowJobsRunningTTL` 10s. A finished run can still change, because a **RE-RUN is a different set of jobs**, so both kinds carry the owning `run_id`. A `workflow_run` delivery flushes every row under that run, as does a job delivery the stored page cannot absorb.

  One naming a job the page does not list, or carrying a different `run_attempt` (repo-wide when the payload names no run). `repository` flushes repo-wide. Depth: docs/webhooks/invalidations.md. Rebuild: `{total_count, jobs:[…]}` / one job of `{id, run_id, run_attempt, workflow_name, head_branch, head_sha, name, status, conclusion, created_at, started_at, completed_at, labels, runner_name, steps:[{name,status,conclusion,number,started_at,completed_at}]}` — nullables always keyed, every URL field dropped (no consumer survey has pinned one here).

  Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100), `page` (1..10) and `filter`. `filter=latest` is GitHub's default and shares the bare row. `filter=all` lists every attempt's jobs, a different set, so it is stored under its own kind `run_jobs_all` and rewritten by the same deliveries. Any other value passes through. An EMPTY page is stored too, on the queued TTL. It is keyed by the run the path names. It is the answer for a run with no jobs yet, which `gh wait-ci` polls. The first job delivery for the run does not appear on it, so it flushes the run's rows. Together the routes are the second- and fourth-largest unrouted slices of the request log. The alternative leavs quarters of the mirror's passthrough volume permanently uncacheable, with the fleet re-asking GitHub for state. It had already been told.
- `GET /orgs/{org}/installation` + `GET /users/{username}/installation` (`respcache_installation.go`) — the OWNER-level installation lookups answer the same object as the repo-level one for an account rather than a repository. This is on the same App-JWT terms (registered OUTSIDE `requireAuth`, bearer self-verified, keyed by the verified app id). They reuse that route's absorb, rebuild, row space, and invalidation: a row is keyed (app actor, owner, repo). As a result, an owner-level answer is stored under a **sentinel repo value** no real repository can collide with (`*org` / `*user` — `*` is illegal in a GitHub repo name). Sentinels because they are questions: an account can answer one and 404 the other. Invalidated by `installation`/`installation_repositories` on the stored installation id, + 24h TTL.

  **The 404 "not installed here" VERDICT is cached too** (both the owner and repo spellings), on the contents/compare/git-ref precedent. Forwards in one process were authoritative 404s relayed unstored, a fleet sweep re-asking the same accounts forever. `repo_installation_cache` carries `status`/`message` for it. A verdict row has `installation_id` 0, so the by-id flush cannot reach it and the same deliveries additionally sweep every verdict away (`InvalidateAbsentRepoInstallations`). That sweep only covers the mirror's OWN App — a consumer App gaining an installation emits nothing the mirror ever sees. So the REAL bound is the verdict's own TTL, `installationAbsentTTL` (a few minutes), not the 24h a real installation object gets.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels/{name}` (`respcache_labels.go`) — one label DEFINITION ("does auto-pr-merge exist here, and what colour is it"), asked per repo per sweep by pr-minder's label reconciliation: forwards in one process, all of them 200s. Whole-doc rows in `label_cache` keyed by (owner, repo, **VERBATIM requested name**) — GitHub resolves label names case-insensitively. The mirror does not model that, so each spelling is its own row. Rebuild: `{id, node_id, name, color, default, description}` (GitHub's `label` schema minus its one `url`. `description` nullable-but-always-keyed).

  Shape guard: no query parameter and only the default JSON Accept. A label name carrying a slash matches no route segment and keeps passing through, as does the labels LIST. Invalidation is the exact signal, already subscribed and already applied to `pr_labels`: EVERY `label` delivery flushes the repo's rows — the grain is the REPO.

  This is because an edit can RENAME (names in one delivery) and one label answers under every requested spelling — plus `repository` events and a 24h TTL backstop. `PATCH`/`DELETE` on the same path are registered purely to flush BEFORE proxying (the Code Quality trick). A caller cannot read back its own stale write. This is in the seconds before the delivery lands.

  **Only the 200 is stored**: an absent-label verdict will let an ensure-then-create caller read its own stale 404 and create the label twice. This is with every observed answer a 200 it will buy nothing for that risk.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks` + `GET /orgs/{org}/hooks` (`respcache_hooks.go`, one `hooks_cache` row space, scopes `repo`/`org`) — the webhook CONFIGURATION listings, together the largest genuinely unrouted slice after the runs listing (6045 and forwards in one process). GitHub answers both with the same hook object, so one flow serves both. The scope is part of the key, so a repo named like an org can never answer the other question.

  **Keyed by the CREDENTIAL, and here that is the security boundary rather than a convenience.** These are ADMIN-only reads: GitHub refuses them to a caller who can merely READ the repository. The show layer proves exactly that READ access — and its public fast path admits ANY authenticated principal without asking GitHub anything. So a global row behind the ordinary gate will hand a read-only caller the repo's webhook endpoints. A row keyed by the bearer's SHA-256 fingerprint is self-gating. It can only ever be replayed to the exact credential GitHub already answered it for.

  Rebuild: a JSON ARRAY of `{id, type?, name, active, events, config:{url?, content_type?, insecure_ssl?, secret?}, created_at, updated_at, last_response?}`. GitHub's API self-links (`url`, `test_url`, `ping_url`, `deliveries_url`) are dropped. **`config.url` is a pinned no-URL exception on grounds the others do not need**. It is not a link into GitHub's API but the hook's own DESTINATION. The field that says which hook this is, so a listing without it is not a trimmed answer. However, this is a broken one (no consumer survey substitutes for that.

  The endpoint's whole purpose is the config). `secret` preserves PRESENCE exactly (the PR-files stance): GitHub omits it when no secret is set and sends a fixed mask when one is. As a result, the key's presence is itself the answer to "is a secret configured". `insecure_ssl` is documented as a string OR a number and rides as raw JSON rather than being coerced. `last_response` is kept and is honestly TTL-stale: it moves with every delivery. No webhook names the change, but omitting a key a consumer branches on is worse than serving it minutes old.

  Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100) and `page` (1..10) only. Only a 200 ARRAY absorbs. An empty array is a valid cacheable answer (it IS what a reconciliation sweep asks), and a **403 relays unstored and is deliberately not a cached verdict**. A permission grant is exactly the kind of thing that changes with no event reaching the mirror.

  **Invalidation, and the signal that looks right and is not.** GitHub's `meta` event names a hook deletion but is delivered ONLY to the webhook being deleted. As a result, another hook's removal is something the mirror never hears about. It is not a usable signal here, and an earlier version of this document suggested it was. What the mirror does see: a write it PROXIES on these paths (`POST /…/hooks`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /…/hooks/{id}` are registered purely to flush before forwarding, the Code Quality trick) and `repository` events. The write flush drops the target's listings **across every credential**, not just the writer's.

  A hook one caller creates changes what every caller sees, and a reconciler working from a listing that write invalidated will create a duplicate webhook. The TTL bounds everything else, which is therefore a few minutes and is the PRIMARY bound.

- `GET /installation/repositories` (`respcache_installationrepos.go`) — "which repositories does the token I am holding cover": forwards in one process, each caller asking the same single-page question ~17 times. **Keyed by the CREDENTIAL** (a SHA-256 fingerprint of the bearer, not the bearer), not by the reveal-layer principal — the answer is one installation token's own view. This is the `app:<id>` principal deliberately shares one bucket across every token of an app, INCLUDING tokens of different installations. These cover different repositories.

  Per-credential keying is also what gates the row without a show decision. A stored answer can only ever be replayed to the exact credential GitHub already answered it for (the token-mint route's stance — a per-credential answer is not shared truth).

  Rebuild: `{total_count, repository_selection, repositories:[{id, node_id, name, full_name, owner:{login,type}, private, visibility, default_branch, fork, archived, disabled}]}` — `visibility` nullable-but-always-keyed rather than defaulted (an answer that did not carry it must not read as "public"), and the dozens of `*_url` templates GitHub attaches dropped. Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100) and `page` (1..20) only. Only a 200 absorbs. A 401 (the token expired) relays unstored.

  Invalidation: `installation`/`installation_repositories` flush the WHOLE table (rows key a credential, so there is no installation id to match on, and the deliveries are rare) — but the mirror receives only its own App's. As a result, the real bound is the 15-minute TTL, `installationReposTTL`. The route sits INSIDE `requireAuth`, a deliberate change for a path that used to skip it.

  A credential requireAuth rejects now gets the mirror's 401/503 rather than GitHub's own answer, which only affects calls that cannot succeed upstream anyway.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/commits` (`respcache_pullcommits.go`) — GitHub answers it with the SAME item shape as the repository commits list. As a result, this route **reuses that storage whole**: the listed commits are upserted into the one global `git_commits_cache`. This is the page's ordered shas become a `commits_list_cache` snapshot under the synthetic ref key `pull/<number>/commits`. That is the resource those rows already model (an ordered list of commits under a key). It inherits the immutable-commit synergy, the hit gate (every listed sha must still resolve), the pruning, and the rebuild unchanged. A caller cannot collide with the key, which will require `?sha=pull/<n>/commits` on the repo commits list — a ref that resolves to nothing. This is never stored. Show uses the single-PR route's deny kind and resource key (same resource, same authorization question). Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100) and `page` (1..10) only. Invalidation follows the PR-files route, which has the same fork-head problem. Every `pull_request`/`pull_request_review` delivery flushes that ONE PR, a `push` flushes the repo's PR-commit snapshots as the belt for a missed delivery. This is `repository` repo-wide, + the shared 24h TTL. The dispatcher restates the key literal (a sync -> api import will be a cycle). Both sides pin it and an end-to-end flush test proves they meet.

- `GET /app` + `GET /user` + `GET /user/orgs` (`respcache_identity.go`) — the identity/self routes. NOT the trimmed-rebuild contract every other route here follows: `TestProxy_FormerlyCachedNowForwarded` (`proxy_test.go`) records why. An earlier trimmed `/user` cache broke a consumer reading a field the model dropped. The fix reverts to raw passthrough rather than guessing a subset again. These three instead follow **"identical-or-passthrough"**: the upstream body is cached VERBATIM (no decode, no re-marshal). As a result, a hit is byte-identical to a live fetch.

  The JWT's VERIFIED app id (`ghcl registers /app`ient.VerifyAppIdentity`, itself cached per-JWT) rather than the JWT itself. A caller minting a fresh JWT per request still pays verification's own `GET /app` call every time (this is NOT the missing-offline-verification gap closed — GitHub still has to attest the JWT), but a caller reusing one JWT.

  This is for repeated calls, or a second app whose document is already warm, pays nothing further. The bearer's fingerprint keys /user`/`/user/orgs`, inside requireAuth. None of the three carry a webhook signal (no delivery names "my own profile changed"), so `IdentityCacheTTL` (30 min) is the only bound. Absorb gate: a 200 that parses as an object with a positive `id` (`/app`, `/user`) or as an array (`/user/orgs`, an empty array valid).

  Any query string or non-default Accept passes through.
- `GET /orgs/{org}/actions/runners` (`respcache_orgrunners.go`) — the live self-hosted-runner roster (admin-scoped: GitHub refuses it below `admin` on the org). Keyed by the bearer's fingerprint, the `hooks_cache` precedent (a global row behind the ordinary show gate will leak an admin-only answer to a merely-authenticated caller), cached VERBATIM. No webhook announces a runner going online/offline/busy. As a result, the TTL is short (30s) and primary. A `workflow_job` delivery's `runner_name`/`runner_id` on in_progress/completed can in principle patch a listed runner's live-ness. However, the listing's shape (labels, busy, status per runner) is wider than what a job delivery states. As a result, this stays TTL-bound rather than derived. Shape guard: `per_page`/`page` only.
- `GET /app/installations` (`respcache_appinstallations.go`) — the App's own installation listing, registered OUTSIDE requireAuth like the mint/installation-lookup routes (JWT-verified, keyed by the verified app id). Cached VERBATIM per page. Unlike the org-runners roster, this DOES have a clean webhook signal: every `installation`/`installation_repositories` delivery carries the installation's own `app_id`. As a result, the dispatcher flushes exactly that app's pages (`ParseInstallationAppID` + `InvalidateAppInstallationsForApp`) — never every app's, and never a blanket invalidate-and-refetch. TTL (1h) is the backstop for a missed delivery.
- `GET /user/repos` (`respcache_userrepos.go`) — the personalized repo listing spanning every repo the token can see, across every owner (distinct from the org-scoped GraphQL tier-1 query). Keyed by the bearer's fingerprint + `sort`/paging, cached VERBATIM (a repo's `permissions` object is exactly the kind of field a trim guesses incorrect about with no consumer survey). No webhook interaction: a token's own visible-repo set changing has no single delivery that states it, so TTL (5 min) is the only bound. Shape guard: `sort` (one of GitHub's documented values) + paging. `affiliation`/`visibility`/`type`/`direction`/`since`/`before` are unmodeled and pass through.
- `GET /search/issues` (`respcache_searchissues.go`) — the documented exception to webhook-driven invalidation (docs/cache/uncacheable-routes.md covers the sibling routes that stay uncached for the same underlying reason): an arbitrary search query names no single resource a payload can patch. Keyed by the bearer's fingerprint + a hash of the modeled shape (`q`, `per_page`, `page` — `q` itself is unbounded text and never stored raw), cached VERBATIM. **`token_fp` is part of the key for correctness, not convenience** — search results are permission-scoped (GitHub filters hits to what the caller's token can see), so a row keyed. This is on query text alone will replay one credential's results to a different, possibly less-privileged credential asking the same query. TTL is short (30s) by design: long enough to collapse a tight poll loop asking the same query. This is short enough that a real answer change is visible within one poll cycle either way. `sort`/`order` are unmodeled and pass through.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{sha}` (`respcache_gittrees.go`) — content-addressed by `sha` like the git-commits cache, so positive rows are immutable: no invalidation, no TTL, LRU-bounded only. Unlike the identity/runner/search routes above, this one DOES trim. A git tree entry's shape (`{path, mode, type, sha, size?}`) is narrow and well-understood, not a wide unsurveyed object. Rebuilt as `{sha, truncated, tree:[{path, mode, type, sha, size?}]}` with every `url` dropped. `recursive=1` is part of the key (a different sha's worth of entries, not a filter on the same set).
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{check_run_id}` (`respcache_checkrun.go`) — the single check-run read, reusing the commit-CI cache's trimmed item shape (`ghdata.TrimCheckRunJSON`) and TTL (24h). **Absorbs directly from `check_run`/`check_suite` deliveries** — the payload's own run object rewrites the row in place (`ApplyCheckRunByID`, called unconditionally ahead of the existing `commit_ci_cache` absorption in `settleCommitCI`), so a webhook never merely invalidates this route. `repository` events and the check-events "no refs" fallback still flush by repo as the belt for an unparseable/refless delivery.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/heads/*` (`respcache_matchingrefs.go`) — the ARRAY form of the ref lookup that `respcache_gitrefs.go`'s single-ref route explicitly declines ("a partial ref makes it answer an ARRAY, a different shape this route does not hold"). Its own row space and TTL (24h). A partial-ref match set can grow or shrink on any push to a matching branch. GitHub gives no cheaper signal than "some ref under this prefix moved", so `push` flushes the repo's rows (alongside the existing branches-list flush) rather than trying to patch one entry. `repository` flushes repo-wide. pr-minder's queue-branch scan is the modeled caller (survey 2026-08-23). Only the `heads/` prefix form is modeled -- GitHub's endpoint takes any `refs/` subtree. However, every observed call names `heads/`, and modeling `tags/` or a bare `refs/` prefix will gueses at a shape nothing here sends. Per-page whole-doc snapshots, the branches_list_cache precedent: a branch create/delete/tip-move all arrive. This is as a push naming a ref under `refs/heads/`. This route has no narrower per-ref target than the branches listing does. As a result, push/repository webhooks flush the whole repo's rows rather than attempting a per-prefix apply. The rebuild trims each entry to `{ref, object: {sha}}` (`url`/`node_id` dropped) -- the one field pr-minder's queue scan reads. An empty array (no ref matches the prefix) is a valid cacheable answer.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-quality/setup` (`respcache_codequality.go`) — GitHub Code Quality's per-repo enablement configuration, a large uncached slice of the request log (a fleet sweep asking "is this repo enrolled", per repo). Modeled from GitHub's OpenAPI description (schema `code-quality-setup`, public preview — [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/code-quality/code-quality#get-a-code-quality-setup-configuration)) rather than from a captured sample. The endpoint takes no query parameters. As a result, the repo is the whole key. The rebuild is the whole documented record — `{state, languages, runner_type, runner_label, updated_at, schedule, ai_findings_option}`. This is because the schema carries no URL field to drop, with every nullable keyed and `languages` always an array. `state: not-configured` is a real cacheable verdict (it IS what the sweep asks). Non-200s (403 "not available here", 404, 503) relay unstored and are deliberately NOT cached as verdicts: unlike a missing git ref, nothing observable says when the feature becomes available.

  **Staleness, stated plainly:** this is CONFIG and GitHub emits no webhook when it changes. The mirror sees exactly one change signal — a `PATCH` to the same path that it proxies, which is why the PATCH is registered at all. The handler flushes the row and then forwards. A caller cannot read its own stale config. (The flush runs BEFORE forwarding on purpose: a failed PATCH that dropped the row costs one miss, while a successful PATCH whose flush was skipped serves a incorrect answer for the whole TTL.) `repository` events flush repo-wide.

  A change made in the UI, or by a client that does not go through the mirror, is invisible until the TTL. This is therefore **1 hour**, not the usual 24.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/readme[/{dir}]` (`respcache_readme.go`) — the largest single passthrough in the 2026-09-07 brief. It forwarded many times, which is 51% of everything that process forwarded. Every one was `unrouted`, and one fleet sweep sent almost all of them. GitHub answers the content object the contents route holds. The rebuild therefore reuses `contentsFileJSON`: `{type, encoding, size, name, path, content, sha}`. It drops `url`, `git_url`, `html_url`, `download_url` and `_links`.

  A row in `readme_cache` keys `(owner, repo, subtree, VERBATIM ref)`. It holds the rendered document and the status that document answers with. **The absent verdict IS stored**, unlike the single-label route. Of those answers, 759 were absent. The verdict is about the README and not about the repo. It thus cannot mislead an ensure-then-create caller the way a missing label can.

  Without it, a repo that has no README pays an upstream call on every sweep, forever. The path names a DIRECTORY. So `path` and `name` come from the payload, not from the request. Invalidation is the contents route's own signal, at the same grain. A push flushes each requested ref spelling. It also flushes the `''` spelling when the pushed ref is the default branch.

  It flushes repo-wide when the payload does not name the default branch. A `repository` event flushes repo-wide. `ReadmeCacheTTL` (6h) backstops a lost delivery. Shape guard: the `ref` parameter and nothing else, and the default JSON Accept only. The raw and html representations are a different document. They keep forwarding. A **451** (the repository is blocked) is stored too, as `{message, block:{reason, created_at}}` with `block.html_url` dropped. It is a fact about the repo. A `repository` event drops it.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows` + `/actions/workflows/{id}` (`respcache_workflows.go`) — forwards between them, both `unrouted`. A workflow DEFINITION is not a run. It changes only when a push edits `.github/workflows`. Both grains therefore share `workflows_cache` under a `kind` column, and one repo-wide flush. The single read rebuilds to `{id, node_id, name, path, state, created_at, updated_at, html_url}`. The listing rebuilds to `{total_count, workflows:[...]}`.

  The rebuild drops `url` and `badge_url`. It keeps **`html_url`**, the workflow-runs precedent. That field is the only handle a consumer has for a link back to GitHub. The surveyed caller polls runs, jobs and annotations alongside these, so it reads a workflow to follow it. It does not render a badge. The `{id}` segment is stored VERBATIM.

  GitHub accepts a numeric id or a file name there. Resolving one spelling into the other needs the very answer this caches, so each spelling keys its own row. **Repo-wide is the finest flush grain that exists here.** A push names changed FILES. A map from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to workflow a later id needs the listing this table is the cache of. A repo holds few workflows.

  The wide flush therefore costs little. `WorkflowsCacheTTL` (6h) backstops a lost delivery. Shape guard: paging on the listing, which is every parameter the endpoint documents. The single read takes no parameter at all. A deeper path, such as `/runs` or `/dispatches`, matches no route segment and keeps forwarding.
- **The shared answer table** (`repo_answer_cache` in `schema_plain.sql`, `respcache_repoanswer.go` + `ghdata/respcache_repoanswers.go`). Several repo-scoped routes store one whole rendered answer per request and differ only in how they absorb it. They share one row space under a `kind` column and one read path, `serveRepoAnswer`. This is the show gate, the caller's own stored refusal, the hit, the fetch, the absorb. A row holds a status and a document. A `302` row's document holds the `Location`, which the hit serves with no body. Every other status serves the document. `subject` names what a delivery flushes the row by. `expires_at` is per row. A non-rate-limited **403** from GitHub on any of these routes is the caller's credential lacking a permission. It is stored per principal in the deny cache (`respcache_verdicts.go`), not in the shared row, and the route may name further per-principal statuses. `repository` events flush the repo's rows of every kind.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/logs` + `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs` (`respcache_redirects.go`, kinds `run_logs`/`job_logs`). GitHub answers with a 302 to a signed blob location that expires on its own clock. The route fetches WITHOUT following the redirect (`fetchUpstreamNoRedirect`) and stores the `Location` until the expiry the location states, less `redirectExpiryMargin`. `signedURLExpiry` reads an Azure SAS `se`, an S3 `X-Amz-Date` plus `X-Amz-Expires`, or a unix `Expires`. A location with no expiry it can read, or one already inside the margin, relays unstored. A **410** (logs expired) is a stored verdict for `logsGoneTTL`. A 404 is stored per principal. A 415 and anything else relay. No delivery moves a log location. The expiry is the whole bound. Shape guard: no query parameter, and the default JSON Accept. This also covers `text/plain` passes through.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}` (`respcache_commit.go`, kind `commit`) — the single commit read, reached through the `/commits/*` subtree dispatcher when the tail has no slash. A slashed tail is ambiguous between a branch name and a deeper path such as `/pulls`, so it forwards. Rebuild: `{sha, node_id, commit:{author, committer, message, tree:{sha}, comment_count, verification}, author, committer, parents:[{sha}], stats, files:[{sha, filename, status, additions, deletions, changes, patch?, previous_filename?}]}`. Accounts trim to `{login, id, type}`, and the PRESENCE of `patch` and `previous_filename` is kept exactly. Every URL field is dropped. A document over relays unstored. The ref is the key, verbatim. A full 40-hex sha is immutable and lives `commitImmutableTTL` (many days), LRU-pruned. A branch name or an abbreviated sha lives `commitRefTTL` (5 min). Its row's subject is the ref, so a push or a create/delete for that ref drops every spelling of it. The push payload does not carry the new commit's files or stats. The row cannot be written from it. A **422** (no commit for that ref) is a stored verdict for `commitVerdictTTL`. A 404 is stored per principal. The diff and patch Accepts and any query (the files listing paginates) pass through.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/branches-where-head` (kind `branches_where_head`) — required-builds-manager asks it per commit. Rebuild: a bare array of `{name, commit:{sha}, protected}`. The sha must be full hex. The row's subject is the sha. A push APPLIES what it can: the branch moved OFF `before`. It is removed from `before`'s answer in place (`RemoveBranchHead`). The branch moved ONTO `after`. However, the new entry needs its `protected` flag, which no push states, so `after`'s answer flushes. A branch `delete` removes the branch from every answer in place. A branch `create` names no sha, so every answer flushes. `ghdata.BranchesWhereHeadTTL` (1h) backstops a lost delivery.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{check_run_id}/annotations` (`respcache_annotations.go`, kind `annotations`) — `gh wait-ci` and the gh CLI read it per failed job. Rebuild: a bare array of `{path, start_line, end_line, start_column, end_column, annotation_level, title, message, raw_details}`, nullables keyed. This also covers `blob_href` is dropped. Shape guard: `per_page` and `page` only. The row's subject is the check run id. Every `check_run` delivery for that id drops it, because the payload carries only `annotations_count`. The TTL reads the single check-run row: a run stored as completed gets a day, anything else a couple of minutes. A 403 (a fine-grained token without `checks: read`) and a 404 are stored per principal.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}` (`respcache_branchrules.go`, kind `branch_rules`) — the rules in force on a branch, asked by an App per repo. The branch is a wildcard, because names carry slashes, and is the key verbatim. Rebuild: a bare array of `{type, ruleset_source_type, ruleset_source, ruleset_id, parameters?}`, with `parameters` kept whole when present. Shape guard: `per_page` and `page` only. A `repository_ruleset` delivery drops the repo's rows, or every row of the owner for an organization ruleset. The App must subscribe to that event (`ghdata.RequiredWebhookEvents`). `ghdata.BranchRulesTTL` (1h) backstops it.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags` (`respcache_tags.go`, kind `tags`) — forwards in the 2026-10-12 brief, most of them 404s for a repo that does not exist and 401s for a bad credential. Rebuild: a bare array of `{name, commit:{sha}, node_id}`. This also covers `zipball_url`, `tarball_url` and `commit.url` are dropped. Shape guard: `per_page` (1..100) and `page` (1..10) only, canonicalized so a reordered query is the same row. A 404 is stored per principal (the show probe usually answers it first). A 401 relays unstored. Freshness: a tag push that MOVES a tag rewrites its entry in place from `after` (`ApplyPushedTagTip`). A created or deleted tag, by push or by a `create`/`delete` delivery, flushes the repo's tags pages. This is because the listing's page for a name is not in any payload. A branch push touches nothing. `ghdata.TagsCacheTTL` (24h) backstops a lost delivery.

- `GET /orgs/{org}/repos` + `GET /users/{username}/repos` (`respcache_ownerrepos.go`) — forwards, both `unrouted`. A row keys the bearer's fingerprint alongside the owner. This is the `user_repos_cache` precedent, for the same reason. Each route answers "the repos of this owner that THIS token can see". A shared row therefore replays one credential's private repos to another credential. Per-credential keying is self-gating, so neither route takes a show check of its own.

  `scope` is part of the key and never a synonym. The spellings answer differently for the same name, because a user listing omits an organization's own repos. This route DOES trim, unlike `/user/repos`. It can reuse a shape that is already surveyed. Each entry is the bare-repo route's `repoMetaJSON`. A repo thus reads identically whether a caller asked for it alone or in a listing.

  **Every listed repo is absorbed into `repos` truth on the way past.** That is `webhook.ParseRepositoryObject` plus `UpsertRepo`, the same mapping webhooks and the show probe use. A listing therefore warms the bare-repo route and the show layer's public fast path for free. A partial entry relays the whole page verbatim rather than rendering a hole. Unknown visibility is the case that matters. It fails closed.

  The absent verdict is stored: "this name is not an owner of this kind" is a stable answer. 46 of multiple org-listing answers were absent. Invalidation: a `repository` event flushes the owner's rows across every credential, because the delivery names no token. `OwnerReposCacheTTL` (10 min) is the primary bound. Shape guard: `sort`, `direction` and paging, of GitHub's documented values. The `type` filter is unmodeled and passes through.

## Still forwarding — open work, not verdicts

There is no "correctly uncached" outcome (operator ruling): *"never encourage bypassing the cache for any reason. Bypassing the cache is a hack that means we need something fixed in github-state-mirror."* A route that still forwards is unfinished, and a resource no delivery names. Today is a missing invalidation signal to go add — not a reason to stop. This section records what each still needs. As a result, the next pass starts from the open question rather than rediscovering the route.

This list used to open with the runner coordinator's queued-backlog poll, written up as permanently uncacheable because "a real-time work queue has no webhook naming the change". It did: `check_suite`/`check_run`/`workflow_job` deliver both edges of `queued`. The shape is cached now (above). Read the rest with that in mind.

Volumes below are from the 2026-08-09 implementation brief (915,259 requests in one process. 191,547 of them passthroughs). That capture predates the repo-wide runs listing landing, so its largest entry — 152,581 forwards of `/actions/runs` under `unmodeled-query` — is already closed by the route above. That capture is not repeated here.

- ~~`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` (forwards) and `/actions/jobs/{id}` (9125) while a job is queued or in progress~~ — **done**, and not the way this entry proposed. It called for rebuilding the answer from the `workflow_jobs` TRUTH table. This will needed the queued edge recorded, a couple of new columns, and a completeness marker. None of that was necessary: the delivery already carries the whole job object. As a result, the stored ANSWER is rewritten from it. The fetch supplies the membership a truth table will needed a marker to prove. The caveat this entry raised — a job's `steps` advance mid-run with NO delivery. As a result, only a not-yet-started job rebuilds faithfully — was the load-bearing part. It is why the live TTL is three-way rather than one number. See the route above.
- **A SHARED row for the hook listings.** Both are cached now (above), but per credential, so credentials asking about the same repo each still pay their own fetch. Sharing one row needs an admin oracle. GitHub has two: `permissions.admin` on the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` object the show probe ALREADY fetches, and — for an installation token — the installation's own permission set. This the mirror already caches on the mint and repo-installation routes. Either is a new grant dimension rather than a tweak, **and the arithmetic decides whether it is worth one**. The org listing is asked several times per credential across a handful of orgs, so the repeats the shared row will collect are the ones. This is the per-credential rows already collapse. The repo listing looks like rotating credentials reading each repo exactly ONCE, and against that shape a global row gated. This is on a per-(credential, repo) probe costs accurately the upstream call it saves. Only a proof earned ONCE PER CREDENTIAL — the installation's permission set, not a per-repo probe — can pay there. Measure the distinct-repo count from a fresh brief before building it. The ~118×1 reading is inferred from caller counts, not from repo counts the brief carries.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` filtered by `event`/`actor`/ `created` — the same route, the same invalidation. These filters simply have no observed traffic to survey. As a result, they are not in the key yet. Adding one is a validator plus a key component.
- `GET /app/hook/deliveries` — deliberately left uncached. See docs/cache/uncacheable-routes.md.

The brief adds these, and none of them is a verdict:

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{ref}` where the ref is a BRANCH NAME (forwards, `unmodeled-path`, spread over `master`, `main` and `dev`). The route models a full-hex sha only, because a tree row is content-addressed and immutable. A branch name is not. Closing this needs the branch tip. The mirror already keeps one: `KnownBranchTip` plus the stale-tip repair in docs/cache/stale-tip-repair.md. The open question is the second hop. A tip is a COMMIT sha, and this route keys a TREE sha. As a result, the answer needs the commit object between them. Do not answer it with a mutable row keyed on the branch name.

Routes closed since the 2026-08-09 brief that this section no longer lists (moved to "The routes" above, each with its actual invalidation signal): `GET /app` + `GET /user` + `GET /user/orgs`, `GET /orgs/{org}/actions/runners`, `GET /app/installations`, `GET /user/repos`, `GET /search/issues`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{sha}`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{check_run_id}`, and `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/heads/…`.

Closed since the 2026-09-07 brief: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/readme`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows[/{id}]`, `GET /orgs/{org}/repos`, and `GET /users/{username}/repos`.
